exposure: Postpartum pelvic floor musculature training program
outcome: Urinary incontinence impact on quality of life
cohort: The study included 28 rooming-in women in the puerperal period at a Maternity School.
finding: A pelvic floor muscle exercise program significantly improved sexual function, reduced the impact of urinary incontinence on quality of life, and increased the pressure of pelvic floor muscles in puerperal women.
mod_finding: There was no significant time-versus-group interaction between delivery type (vaginal vs. cesarean) and the improvements observed in sexual function, impact of urinary incontinence, or pressure of pelvic floor muscles.
